title.narrative: ROAP/FIJ Accelerating Multi Level Action for SDG Localization in Fiji

description.narrative:
Short description: The joint programme delivers a comprehensive approach to accelerate development planning and multi-level governance for the localization of the SDGs in Fiji. By engaging stakeholders and building capacities at multiple levels, it seeks to transform Fiji’s cities and towns for improved livability, inclusivity, and sustainability for all. The joint programme directly supports the implementation of Fiji’s 2023 Voluntary National Review report’s recommendations regarding SDG localization and the Pacific UNSDCF, contributing to all pillars (Planet, People, Prosperity and Peace).
Context: In response to the priority for Fiji to localize the SDGs as stated in its 2023 VNR Report, and the growing need to integrate the SDGs at the heart of multi-level governance, planning and investment strategies, the following Theory of Change outlines a comprehensive approach that leverages technical assistance, stakeholder engagement, and capacity building to foster SDG-aligned local development at community, municipal and national levels. The project proposal is aligned with the Pacific UNSDCF, and 15 contributes to all pillars (Planet, People, Prosperity and Peace) in particular, (under pillar 1, Planet) 1.2.1 Enhanced climate resilient policies and infrastructure for basic services, food systems, human mobility and settlements (under pillar 3, prosperity) 3.2.1 Strengthened institutional capacity to design and implement holistic policies to foster blue, green and creative economy at national and regional level.
Partnerships, often referred to as the “fifth pillar” of the Pacific UNSDCF, are reflected as a cross-cutting priority and will be leveraged to reach those groups of people at risk of being left behind, including women and people with disabilities. In this context, the joint programme considers a human rights-based approach to development solutions and building urban resilience.
Outcome Statement: Empower cities and towns in Fiji to create more inclusive, resilient, and sustainable communities by effectively integrating SDGs and their key transitions into local development planning, financing and action supported by enhanced capacity of local stakeholders for no one to be left behind.
Expected key results of the Joint Programme: - Enhanced integration of SDGs into municipal development plans - Enhanced enabling environment of national and local actors to integrate and implement SDGs - Enhanced institutional capacities capacity at local level to put SDG acceleration plans into action
